THE EVIDENCE / QUESTIONS BEFORE CONCLUSIONS

Every finding has a trail.

Questions, denominators, and decisions travel together. An association or a simulation cannot establish a causal effect.

FORECAST EVALUATION

Does the network add value?

Inspect evaluation ↗

Chronological evaluation on unseen dates. Lower MAE and RMSE are better; higher severe-event recall is better.
ModelEvaluationMAE ⓘRMSECalibrationSevere recallRuntime

MAE: mean absolute error. RMSE: root mean squared error. Errors are in percentage points. Calibration compares mean predicted and observed rates in ten bins. Recall is the share of ≥50%-disruption cases detected.

KNOW THE BOUNDARY

Useful evidence.
Explicit assumptions.

CASCADE reconstructs one carrier’s public reporting record. It is a research replay of information availability, not a live airline control system.

01

At the cutoff

Scheduled volume, recent observed departures, and lagged weather enter the forecast. Final delay causes and future actual aircraft assignments do not. Historical event and weather latencies are declared assumptions.

02

After the fact

Validated same-tail links trace plausible propagation. Missing tails, diversions, inconsistent times, and broken airport continuity break the chain. Shared aircraft alone cannot prove why a flight was late.

03

Inside the simulation

Observed schedules and retrospective aircraft chains bound the experiment. Passenger connections, crew legality, maintenance, and real recovery costs are unavailable and are not invented.

04

Back to the source

SQL tables, source hashes, model runs, and evaluation reports make the displayed results inspectable. Empty values remain missing, and cancelled flights remain in the disruption denominator.
